items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to the establishment of procedures or mechanisms to receive allegations of abuse or mistreatment of patients served by programs licensed or operated under the mental hygiene law and repealing certain provisions of such law relating thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A9825                 REVISED 3/1/10

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to
the establishment of procedures or mechanisms to receive allegations
of abuse or mistreatment of patients served by programs licensed or
operated under the mental hygiene law and repealing certain provisions
of such law relating thereto

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL: To establish toll free numbers for
the reporting of abuse of persons with disabilities being served by
agencies and providers licensed or operated under the mental hygiene
law,

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS: Subdivision 6 of section 29.29 of the
mental hygiene law is repealed and a new subdivision 6 is added as
described in the bill; and paragraph of subdivision (c) of section
45.07 of the mental hygiene law, as amended by chapter 323 of the laws
of 2008, is amended as described in the bill.

JUSTIFICATION: Last year, both houses of our legislature unanimously
approved legislation (A.8972-A/S.5930-A) creating a toll free hotline
to report the abuse or mistreatment of adults with developmental and
or mental disabilities who are served by state licensed and state
operated residential care facilities. Citing fiscal concerns and
duplication of some existing hotlines, the Governor vetoed the bill
last year.

Since that time; a series of meetings have taken place with the
Governor's office and state agencies. This new bill contains parts of
compromise language that will enable the Commissioners of the relevant
agencies to establish procedures for a hotline. While some of the
state agencies currently operate toll-free hotlines, their existence
is not in law and not statutorily required. This bill would remedy
that situation.

Some of our state's mentally disabled adults have cognitive
functioning that is less than a non-disabled child. This makes them
vulnerable to abuse in situations where they are unable to speak for
themselves or to successfully relate an incident. The creation of a
hotline will better ensure the reporting of abuse and suspected abuse
of these vulnerable individuals, who are adults by law, but lack many
of the adult skills necessary to advocate for themselves in an abusive
situation.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: A.8972-A/S.5930-A of 2009 (Veto
#44 of 2009)

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: Minimal, but undetermined.

EFFECTIVE DATE: Effective on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

summary: Requires the establishment of procedures or mechanisms to receive allegations of abuse or mistreatment of patients served by programs licensed or operated under the mental hygiene law; includes allegations received anonymously; requires toll-free number.
